_note: Granular question types, derived bottom-up from the College Board educator bank by reading cropped question IMAGES (the maths is rendered, not text). One agent per CB skill, capped at 3-6 types, so the total is bounded arithmetically rather than by an adjective. Counts are out of a 12-question concentrated sample per skill; full-bank counts come from the assignment pass.

primitives.name: read a factored form
primitives.what: (x-r)(x-s) hands you the zeros r and s directly, and the vertex sits at their midpoint (r+s)/2. A zero in a table or on a graph means that factor. Never expand to find any of these -- expanding is the slow way to the thing the form is already telling you.
appears_in: Vieta - sum or product of the roots

primitives.name: undo a square or an absolute value into two cases
primitives.what: A square and an absolute value both DESTROY the sign, so undoing one always gives TWO cases, and the relation decides which two. |A|=k -> A=k or A=-k. sqrt(A^2)=|A|, not A. x^2<k -> -sqrt(k)<x<sqrt(k), a BAND. x^2>k -> x<-sqrt(k) or x>sqrt(k), TWO TAILS. Never carry a +/- into an inequality: 'b < +/-52' is not a statement. Write the band or the tails first, THEN apply the question's own constraints (positive, integer, greatest).
